cohort: The study included nulliparous women with singleton term fetuses in vertex presentation, intact membranes, and an unfavorable cervix (Bishop score < 6) who underwent cervical ripening.
finding: The cervical-ripening balloon (CRB) was more effective than the dinoprostone vaginal insert (PG) in increasing cervical consistency and dilatation, while their efficacy for vaginal delivery was similar.
mod_finding: The efficacy of CRB and PG for vaginal delivery was similar, and no Bishop score criterion was found to be a significant predictor for vaginal delivery.
